items.title: Maruti Q1 results: What could lead to a profit decline for India's largest carmaker?
items.description: Maruti Suzuki is expected to post strong Q1FY27 revenue growth of 31% YoY, driven by robust volumes and better realisations. However, the average estimates of six brokerages point to a 7% decline in net profit as higher commodity costs, increased discounts and lower other income weigh on margins. Investors will closely watch management commentary on demand, pricing and margin outlook.

items.title: M&M Q1 Results: Standalone profit rises 7% YoY to Rs 3,685 crore; revenue jumps 23%
items.description: Mahindra and Mahindra reported a seven percent net profit rise for the June quarter. Consolidated profit after tax increased thirty-four percent, driven by strong business growth. The auto business saw volumes rise twenty-three percent, retaining its SUV market leadership. Tractor volumes grew eighteen percent, maintaining the top position in the segment. Services revenue and profit also experienced significant year-on-year increases.

items.title: ITC Q1 Preview: Will cigarette tax shock drag profit lower despite FMCG strength?
items.description: ITC is expected to report a weak Q1FY27 as the first full-quarter impact of the new cigarette tax regime weighs on volumes and profitability. While the FMCG business is likely to deliver healthy growth, brokerages expect pressure from cigarettes and the agri segment to drag overall revenue, EBITDA and profit.

items.title: Swiggy Q1 Results: Net loss narrows to Rs 791 crore; revenue jumps 37% YoY
items.description: Swiggy Q1 Results: The online food and grocery delivery platform reported a 37% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 6,812 crore in the April–June quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 4,961 crore in the year-ago period.

items.title: Hyundai Motor Q1 Results: Profit slumps 35% YoY to Rs 889 crore as headwinds weigh on volumes
items.description: Hyundai Motor India reported a net profit of Rs 889 crore for Q1 FY27. This represents a significant 35% decrease from the previous year's earnings. Revenue from operations saw a slight dip to Rs 16,335 crore. EBITDA also tumbled 31% year-on-year to Rs 1,512 crore. The company experienced a challenging quarter due to multiple headwinds.

items.title: Bajaj Finance Q1 Results: Profit jumps 28% YoY to Rs 6,081 crore, NII surges 23%
items.description: Bajaj Finance on Thursday reported 28% year-on-year (YoY) growth in its standalone net profit at Rs 6,081 crore, compared with Rs 4,765 crore in the last year quarter. Net interest income in the reporting period increased 23% YoY to Rs 12,571 crore.

items.title: Vedanta Q1 Results: Profit jumps 72% YoY to Rs 5,473 crore; EBITDA soars 98% to record high
items.description: Vedanta's net profit surged seventy-two percent year-on-year for the first quarter. Revenue from operations also increased fifty-four percent during the same period. The company's EBITDA soared ninety-eight percent to its highest level ever. EBITDA margin improved significantly, excluding the copper business segment. These strong financial results reflect a robust performance for Vedanta.

items.title: Vedanta Aluminium Q1 Results: Net profit soars 3x YoY to Rs 5,629 crore; Rs 8/share dividend declared
items.description: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Q1 Results: Vedanta Aluminium reported a more than threefold jump in Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit to Rs 5,629 crore, while revenue rose 46% YoY to Rs 21,393 crore in its first quarterly results since the demerger. The company also announced its maiden interim dividend of Rs 8 per share, as shares gained 2% following the earnings announcement.

items.title: IRB Infrastructure Q1 profit zooms 51% YoY to Rs 306 crore
items.description: IRB Infrastructure has reported a remarkable 51 percent profit increase for the June quarter, bolstered by strong revenue figures. The company experienced a modest rise in total income compared to last year's performance. Additionally, they announced an interim dividend of sixty crore rupees, reaffirming their commitment to achieving asset growth goals.

items.title: Tata Steel Q1 Results: Profit rises 15% to Rs 2,318 crore, revenue climbs 14%
items.description: Tata Steel reported a 15% year-on-year rise in Q1 consolidated net profit to Rs 2,318 crore, driven by higher revenue and stronger operating performance. Revenue grew 14%, while profit before tax increased despite higher expenses and exceptional restructuring-related charges during the quarter.

items.title: Ambuja Cements Q1 net profit down 37% as sales volume slips
items.description: Ambuja Cements reported a profit drop, impacted by lower sales volume and higher costs. The company will now prioritize value over sales volume in its operations. Consolidated net profit decreased by thirty-seven percent year-on-year during the fiscal first quarter. Higher imported fuel prices and trade costs affected industry profitability significantly. Ambuja Cements remains confident of outpacing industry growth for the remainder of the fiscal.

items.title: Hyundai India Q1 profit misses estimates, drops 35% on disruptions
items.description: Hyundai Motor India reported a 35% decline in Q1 net profit, missing estimates as production disruptions and weaker Middle East exports hurt earnings. The company expects recovery from Q2 with production normalisation, new vehicle launches and Rs 7,500 crore planned capital expenditure.

items.title: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Q1 Results: Profit rises 3% to Rs 566 crore
items.description: Torrent Pharmaceuticals announced a robust profit after tax of Rs 566 crore for the first quarter, showcasing impressive growth. Revenue soared to Rs 4,921 crore, with Indian revenue up by nineteen percent and a significant thirty-six percent increase in US revenue. Meanwhile, Germany and Brazil experiences growth of three and twenty-seven percent, respectively. The strong financial performance reflects the success of new launches and market opportunities.

items.title: NSE Q1 Results: Profit rises 7% YoY to Rs 3,120 crore; revenue up 9%
items.description: National Stock Exchange reported a seven percent profit rise for the June quarter. Higher transaction charges and strong operating margins contributed to this financial growth. Consolidated total income also saw a nine percent increase year-on-year. The exchange is currently preparing for its proposed initial public offering. NSE's contribution to the exchequer reached over twenty thousand crore rupees.
